correctness.rationale: The Fourier decomposition has distinct eigenvalues in every 2x2 block and every modal eigenvector has a nonzero outer-layer component. At each eigenvalue, outer restrictions of the contributing Fourier basis to the first m outer vertices form a nonsingular Vandermonde matrix, so r=max spectral multiplicity inputs suffice by PBH; eigenspace dimension supplies the matching lower bound. The Chebyshev leading term yields the 2k+2 cap. The GP(11,2) resultant is exact and squarefree modulo two. Finite modular Kalman computations support the illustrations, not the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The original spectral formula and 2k+2 zero-forcing outer prefix are credited. The asserted novel fact is a uniformly minimum, multiplicity-adaptive consecutive OUTER coordinate-input placement for the fixed Laplacian on all generalized Petersen parameters, with residual literature-priority risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed specialist network-sampling or I-graph control paper might present the same consecutive-outer minimum theorem.
The Fourier/PBH/Vandermonde deduction is short and uses established spectrum results; novelty is the explicit joint placement claim, not an invention of those methods.
